The automatic path starts in [src/instrumentation.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/instrumentation.ts). On the Node.js runtime, `register()` registers event handlers and calls `startScheduler()`. In [scheduler.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/jobs/scheduler.ts), the scheduler ticks every minute; `tick()` considers the `overdue-issues` job due on its first tick and then at a 60-minute cadence. It enqueues the job and drains the queue. `runHandler()` in [queue.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/jobs/queue.ts) dispatches it to `runOverdueIssueJob(new Date())`. There is also a direct trigger: `POST()` in [the overdue cron route](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/app/api/cron/overdue/route.ts) checks the cron secret and calls the same job.

`runOverdueIssueJob()` in [overdue-issue-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/jobs/overdue-issue-job.ts) first checks that archived records are filtered, converts the supplied time to a timestamp, and obtains up to 50 organization IDs using `listOrgIdsForRollup()` in [usage-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/repositories/usage-repository.ts). That query selects IDs from usage records ordered by measurement time; the job does not paginate beyond that batch. For each organization, `listOverdueIssues()` in [issue-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/repositories/issue-repository.ts) selects only its unarchived issues with a non-null `dueAt` strictly earlier than the supplied time and status `backlog`, `todo`, `in_progress`, or `in_review`, ordered by due date. Thus closed issues and issues due exactly at the check time do not qualify.

For each result, the job emits an `issue.overdue` event containing the organization, issue, project, due date and nullable assignee, with a null actor. Its responsibility is to announce the fact; it does not choose notification channels or send an alert itself. The module-level `reported` set suppresses another emission for an issue ID after `emit()` returns, and `resetOverdueTracking()` clears it for tests. This is **process-local deduplication**, not a durable once-ever guarantee: a restart clears it, and overlapping scans can both pass the set check before either adds the ID. Also, `emit()` in [event-bus.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/lib/event-bus.ts) waits for subscribers but isolates their failures rather than rethrowing them, so the job can mark an issue reported even if notification handling failed.

The subscriber is installed when [event-registry.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/services/event-registry.ts) imports [notification-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/services/notification-service.ts). Its `registerFanOut()` handler ignores an unassigned issue; otherwise it calls `notify()` for exactly `assigneeId`, with kind `issue_overdue`, an issue link, and a null actor. `notify()` looks up that recipient’s preference for that kind, uses `resolveChannels()` to select channels, and skips the recipient if none remain. With no saved preference, the default is `in_app` and `email`; with a preference, the code uses its `inApp` and `email` fields, with the `digest_email` feature flag also affecting email when `digestOnly` is set. It then calls `insertNotifications()` in [notification-repository.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/repositories/notification-repository.ts), which stores a row scoped to that organization and recipient, including the selected channels. `listNotifications()` retrieves rows for a specific recipient.

The fan-out itself creates the notification row; it does not directly send an overdue email. A separate digest path can email unread notifications: `runDigestEmailJob()` in [digest-email-job.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/jobs/digest-email-job.ts) runs at the organization’s configured UTC hour when its digest feature is enabled. It obtains digest subscribers, calls `buildDigest()` in [digest-service.ts](/private/tmp/bench-scratch/d1beae15-e932-4199-982b-e98c9b2d6254/src/server/services/digest-service.ts) for each recipient, renders and sends a nonempty bundle, then marks its entries read. The shown overdue fan-out does not itself provide an immediate email delivery step.
